systematicSearch.scope: Exact COL26.8 identity and a focused review of one primary marker study with publisher-verified article-level reuse terms; this is not a multi-database, seven-facet, or range-wide systematic review.

systematicSearch.inclusionCriteria: Primary-source statements explicitly reporting the 32-individual DNA panel and Alu insertion polymorphism results for the study-labelled S. sciureus and S. boliviensis groups.
systematicSearch.exclusionCriteria: Name-only matches; unverified specimen assignments; range-wide distribution; species-boundary or full phylogenetic conclusions; all unassessed facets; results from separately licensed figures or supplementary files.

claims.text: Within the authors’ 32-individual squirrel-monkey DNA panel, 110 of 382 tested Alu insertion loci were polymorphic for insertion presence or absence; among these, 51 showed the study’s species-informative allele-frequency distributions between its S. sciureus and S. boliviensis groups. The authors note that two specimens labelled S. sciureus clustered more closely with S. boliviensis, so this result is limited to that marker panel and those study assignments and does not independently resolve species boundaries.
claims.locator: Abstract > Results; Methods > DNA samples; Results > Species informative Alu polymorphisms, paragraph preceding Table 4; Table 4; identity caveat in Results > Population structure.
claims.placeTimeScope: Laboratory analyses of a 32-individual mixed-provenance DNA panel; the article does not state collection dates in the cited sections. The result is limited to study-labelled S. sciureus and S. boliviensis groups, with the authors’ specimen-identification caveat retained.
claims.lifeStatus: Tissue and DNA obtained from museums and research centres, with some captive-colony material reported; individual wild/captive status is not resolved for the full panel. No live field observations are used.

gaps: This single marker panel supports a narrow result about recent insertion polymorphisms and sample-group allele-frequency patterns; it does not supply a full species phylogeny, divergence-time estimate, or independently resolved species boundary.
The study’s sample sources are not a range-wide distribution inventory; no native-range or change-through-time claim is made.
No fossil evidence review or bounded fossil-record search was performed.
The paper mentions potential relevance to conservation biology but does not provide a formal status, trend, or population-risk assessment.

reasons: Only one bounded molecular-marker result is supported; six facets remain not-assessed and evolution remains partial.
The sample panel includes historical specimen labels and unresolved individual assignments; no species-boundary conclusion is inferred.
No comprehensive facet-by-facet literature search or independent external expert review has been completed.
